text:
Sam (sales): Quick question from the EU bank POC — they need a concise statement on where customer data is stored/processed during inference. Also asked for a simple dataflow (PII path), KMS usage, and log retention for compliance. Can we share a one-pager + subprocessor list?
Priya (solutions): Short answer: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can pin processing to an EU region and route both inference and logs to the customer's VPC/KMS. For Hosted (standard) we offer EU regions but need to call out subprocessors for cloud infra and any managed logging.
Omar (security): Adding detail: keys can be customer-managed (bring-your-own KMS) on Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with our KMS; customer master keys (CMKs) are supported in EU regions if they have enterprise plan. Log retention: default 30d, can extend with entitlements; for PII/regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private.
Sam (sales): They specifically asked: 1) where tokenized request text lives while in flight; 2) are KV caches persisted to disk and where; 3) are request logs ever exported to third parties; 4) subprocessors list for EU-only hosting.
Jake (cust-eng): Answers inline: 1) In-flight requests are handled in-memory on the serving node in the selected region; short-term KV cache is in-memory by default — persistent caching only when configured (we can disable). 2) We do not write request bodies to disk unless you enable debugging or offline replay; traces/sampled logs can include hashes, not raw content by default. 3) We do not export request logs to external vendors except for our monitoring provider (listable). 4) Subprocessors vary by region — I'll pull the EU hosting subprocessors doc and attach.
Priya (solutions): I'll draft a simple ASCII dataflow they can drop into their vendor review:

```
Client -> TLS -> EU Load Balancer (eu-1) -> Inference Nodes (pinned to eu-1)
  - KV cache (RAM, optional persistent cache -> EU Block Storage)
  - Model weights (local on node / encrypted at rest)
  - Logs -> Logging Service (eu-logs) -> Retention policy: 30d (default) or customer-configured
KMS (customer CMK / Redwood KMS) -> encrypt model checkpoints and any persisted caches/logs
Metrics/alerts -> Monitoring (vendor: listed subprocessor)
```

Omar (security): Add a note: "All egress to other regions requires explicit routing rules. Fallback to non-EU endpoints is blocked by default for EU-pinned deployments." Also: "We can provide a signed attestation for KMS usage and point-in-time key rotation logs if they need audit evidence."
Sam (sales): Perfect. Can you confirm exact subprocessors we should give them for Hosted EU region? They care about monitoring, logging pipeline, and any cloud-managed DB backups.
Jake (cust-eng): Pulling list now — main ones: EU cloud provider (compute/storage), monitoring vendor, observability storage (S3-compatible in eu-1), and an analytics vendor for aggregated usage metrics. None receive raw request bodies by default. I'll paste the named list in a follow-up message and link to our EU subprocessor spreadsheet.
redwood-ops-bot: Deployment eu-1: capacity check OK, current SLA 99.9% for Dedicated clusters in eu-1.
Priya (solutions): Drafted reply for the customer (short): "We can host and process all PII in the EU for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted EU region we restrict processing to selected EU region; subprocessors are limited to EU-region cloud infra and monitoring partners — see attached subprocessor export. KMS options: customer-managed on Dedicated/Private; envelope encryption on Hosted with CMKs in EU available for enterprise. Default log retention is 30 days, extendable. We will provide a simple dataflow diagram and signed KMS attestation on request." Want me to send this as a single PDF to their vendor security team?
Sam (sales): Yes — please attach the ASCII diagram + subprocessor list + the KMS attestation note. Also ask if they want a short tech presales call with Omar and Jake to go through controls (TLS, RBAC, audit logs, backup encryption).
Omar (security): Happy to join. If they request SIG/CAIQ answers we can prod the questionnaire queue and prioritize for a P0 deal.
Jake (cust-eng): Subprocessor doc: https://redwood.internal/sales/eu-subprocessors (shared link). I've also pasted the named list in the follow-up thread.
Sam (sales): Great — I'll send the PDF and set up a 30-min tech call. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
